title: Worksheet 9: Adding and Removing List Items
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Because a list is designed to store a changing collection of values, most programming languages provide built-in tools for adding new items to a list or removing existing items from it after the list has already been created. Adding an item to the end of a list is often called "appending," and it increases the total number of items stored in the list by one. Items can also often be inserted at a specific position within a list, rather than only at the end, shifting the remaining items over to make room for the new one. Removing an item from a list can be done in different ways, such as removing a specific value by name, or removing whatever item is located at a particular index. Whenever an item is added to or removed from a list, the indexes of the remaining items can shift, meaning a value that was previously at index 3 might end up at index 2 after an earlier item is removed, which is an important detail for programmers to keep in mind.
